_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Multi-user lists seed the current-user query once. The browser's requests carry the header X-ExeDev-Email: me@example.com, so the current user is me@example.com. The test harness has already stubbed the server's conversation list and cut off its live update stream, so there is nothing to set up, intercept or check about that (do not look at the API): the drawer (".drawer") shows the conversations the test names, as rows [data-conversation-id="<id>"] whose title (".conversation-title") is their slug, which is their id (drafts have none), and whose preview is "Preview". The list is "mine" (participants collaborator@example.com with 2 messages and me@example.com with 3), "triple" (me@example.com, collaborator@example.com and third@example.com), "other" (other@example.com) and "draft" (a draft, which has no participants). "The search toggle" is the button "Search conversations..."; "the user panel" is data-testid "user-filter-panel", whose options are its [role="option"] elements; "the tooltip" is ".p-tooltip". The visible rows are listed by eval JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll('[data-conversation-id]')].filter(e => { const r = e.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width > 0 && r.height > 0 && e.checkVisibility({visibilityProperty: true}); }).map(e => e.getAttribute('data-conversation-id'))). The search query editor is the contenteditable element with data-testid "conversation-query-editor" ("the editor"); its data-query-value attribute is the serialized query. "The query is X" means data-query-value is exactly X, spaces included. To "set the query to X": eval the editor's focus(), press_key "a" with modifiers "Control" (the editor's own select-all), eval document.execCommand('insertText', false, X), then wait until the query is X. To "clear the query": eval the editor's focus(), press_key "a" with modifiers "Control", press Backspace, then wait until the query is "". Query tokens are [data-conversation-query-token="<kind>"] elements inside the editor (kind tag or user); "the token T" is the one whose text contains T. Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is the element with role button (a <button>) whose accessible name (aria-label, else its text) is exactly X; "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check. Whether an element "has the class X" is an eval of its classList.contains('X') (polled with expect), never a visibility check: a collapsed drawer may have no size. Every selector you need is given here, so do not explore the source code or read other tests (the old Playwright spec is being replaced and does not apply): write all the steps in one run_steps call right away, and look something up only if a step fails. A button "X" is button[aria-label="X"] when one exists (as for "Open conversations", "Search conversations...", "Search tasks...", "View options", "Show chapters", "Archive", "Restore" and "Delete"); otherwise it is the button whose visible text is exactly X, picked with has_text X (a substring match, so make sure no other button's text contains X), as for "Ask Shelley", "View Archived" and "Back to conversations". 1. Navigate to /new. 2. There is no editor. 3. The search toggle has the class "search-toggle-active". 4. [data-conversation-id="mine"] is visible. 5. A draft belongs to whoever is typing it and survives the seeded current-user filter: [data-conversation-id="draft"] is visible. 6. [data-conversation-id="other"] is not visible. 7. The mine row's ".conversation-participant-badge" contains the text "2" and holds exactly one ".conversation-participant-badge-front-filled". 8. Click that badge. 9. The tooltip should contain "collaborator@example.com"; ".p-tooltip strong" has text exactly "me@example.com"; there is exactly 1 ".p-tooltip .conversation-participant-tooltip-identity-current" and exactly 2 ".p-tooltip .conversation-participant-tooltip-identity". 10. Of the ".p-tooltip .conversation-participant-tooltip-row" elements, the first contains "me@example.com" and the second "collaborator@example.com"; the row containing "collaborator@example.com" has no "strong"; the row containing "me@example.com" has a ".conversation-participant-tooltip-count" with text exactly "3". 11. Click the search toggle. 12. The editor's autocapitalize attribute is "none" and its contenteditable attribute is "true". 13. The query is "user:me@example.com ", and the token user:me@example.com is visible. 14. No element has the exact text "@ Participating". 15. Click the button "Add user filter"; the query should be "user:me@example.com user:". 16. Click the button "Add tag filter"; the query should be "user:me@example.com tag:". 17. Click the button "Add user filter"; the query should be "user:me@example.com user:". 18. Press Escape. 19. Record the visible rows in window.__defaultOrder (eval "window.__defaultOrder = " followed by that expression). 20. Click the button "Add user filter". 21. No option of the user panel contains "other@example.com". 22. Click the user panel's option containing "third@example.com". 23. The query should be "user:me@example.com user:third@example.com "; there are exactly 2 user tokens; the token user:third@example.com is visible. 24. Set the query to "user:me@example.com ". 25. The visible rows should be exactly window.__defaultOrder again (poll an eval comparing the two). 26. Click the search toggle. 27. There is no editor; the search toggle does not have the class "search-toggle-active"; [data-conversation-id="other"] is visible. 28. Click the search toggle. 29. The query is "". 30. Clear the query. 31. [data-conversation-id="other"] and [data-conversation-id="draft"] are visible. 32. The other row's button whose accessible name contains "other@example.com" contains the text "1". 33. There are no user tokens. 34. Click the button "Add user filter"; the query should be "user:" and the user panel visible. 35. Click empty header space, left of the actions, to dismiss the panel: click ".drawer-header" at x 24, y 24. 36. There should be no user panel. 37. Click the button "Add user filter"; the user panel is visible. 38. Click the user panel's option containing "me@example.com". 39. The query should be "user:me@example.com "; [data-conversation-id="other"] is not visible. 40. Clear the query. 41. Click the search toggle. 42. There is no editor, and the search toggle does not have the class "search-toggle-active".
